name: sif-a38ba0ab-blind30-ots
instr:
# sif: restoring a reconnaissance command-line tool's behaviour without a test suite

This is a command-line tool that sweeps hosts and web targets for exposures and writes up what it finds. A single run now goes wrong in a lot of small places at once, and almost none of them announce themselves. The repository has received 30 separate undocumented edits. Nothing about the invocations changed and nothing about the targets changed; the same run that used to come out right now comes out wrong, and in several places work that used to be done is refused outright. What follows is what shows up in ordinary use.

Starting the tool the simplest way, with a single target, no settings file and no other switches, the number of concurrent workers comes out as eleven where the built-in default has always been ten; the switches for extra header checking and for injection testing are still off, and no throwaway settings file is left behind. The textual counter that advances as work finishes now moves two steps per finished item, so four finished items leave it reading eight. Asking for a named per-user folder beneath the tool's own data directory hands back an error instead of an absolute path ending in that name under a parent named after the tool, and because of that the piece that reads check definitions off disk cannot be built at all — it used to hand out a built-in folder and a user folder, and now it fails before either.
